items.title: Designing fulfilling and productive workdays: Effects of task meaningfulness sequences on daily engagement and performance.
items.abstract: Given the importance of experiencing fulfilling and productive workdays, scholars have focused on ways to boost employees' daily engagement and performance, suggesting this may be accomplished by increasing meaningfulness of their work tasks. However, an alternative approach may be needed in multifaceted work contexts where employees need to complete sets of varied tasks each day, including tasks that lack meaningfulness. To address this issue, we integrate the workday design perspective with research on residual engagement to examine implications of strategically sequencing tasks in terms of their meaningfulness. We theorize that because of a process we refer to as engagement cascade, performing the day's most highly meaningful tasks earlier and in a concentrated manner will tend to produce higher levels of daily engagement relative to sequences in which the most highly meaningful tasks occur later or are disbursed. We use agent-based modeling to formalize the engagement cascade process and generate specific predictions regarding how daily engagement is impacted by different task meaningfulness sequences. Findings from an intensive longitudinal design study with National Aeronautics and Space Administration and Russian Space Agency crew members (Study 1), an experience sampling field experiment with full-time employees (Study 2), and two controlled laboratory experiments with undergraduates (Study 3 and Supplement to Study 3) provide support for our hypotheses. Specifically, the decreasing task meaningfulness sequence engendered higher levels of daily engagement and, in turn, daily performance, relative to the increasing, inverted U-shaped, and U-shaped sequences. items.title: Designing Learning That Adapts: A practical framework for adaptive, scenario-based learning across classrooms, e-learning platforms and AI-supported education
items.abstract: Designing Learning That Adapts presents a practical framework for adaptive, scenario-based learning that can be applied across classrooms, e-learning platforms and AI-supported education. Drawing on established learning science, instructional design practice and the questions raised by more than a decade of e-learning product work, the paper sets out principles for shaping learning around the learner's goal, starting point, prior knowledge and preferred ways of learning, and for choosing the right mode (text, voice, video, interaction and dialogue) for each task. It frames adaptive and scenario-based approaches as design practices to be observed, tested and revised rather than as proven efficacy claims, and offers a structured way for educators, platform teams and workplace learning designers to apply these ideas in their own contexts. This is a practitioner framework and does not report an empirical efficacy study.

items.title: Designing the Future: Leadership and AI
items.abstract: This chapter explores the evolving, reciprocal relationship between leadership and augmented/artificial intelligence (AI) across individual, team, organizational, and societal levels. While we use the term AI throughout in recognition of its widespread usage, we acknowledge the growing preference for augmented intelligence – a framing advanced by leaders in human–machine teaming, such as Paul G. Kaminski (2020), which emphasizes cognitive extension and human–AI partnership. Just as leadership helped shape – and was reshaped by – the Agricultural, Industrial, and Information Ages, the emerging Age of AI demands a renewed focus on human values and moral courage. Far from a neutral tool, AI reflects the intentions of its designers and the integrity of its leaders, and in turn, transforms how we work, relate, and lead. Grounded in authentic and moral leadership theory, systems thinking, and sociotechnical design, we examine how leaders can engage AI in ways that safeguard human dignity, foster trust, and advance ethical innovation. Through a multilevel lens, we explore how AI influences self-awareness, interpersonal responsibility, team dynamics, and global leadership strategies. We extend prior work on efficacy-performance spirals to the AI context, showing how trust, learning, and adaptation can reinforce or erode across levels over time. Drawing on work published in Organizational Dynamics, this chapter also applies the TRUST, COACH, and CARES frameworks to AI leadership. As AI reshapes decision-making and connection, the defining force will not be technology itself, but the authenticity, trustworthiness, and moral imagination of those who lead it.

items.title: Detecting and Mitigating Query-Based System Prompt Leakage Attacks
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) rely on proprietary system prompts to enforce task directives, safety policies, and access controls. These prompts are vulnerable to query-based leakage attacks, where black-box adversaries extract confidential instructions through adaptive, multi-turn interactions. Existing defenses often assess queries independently, missing malicious behavior that emerges across interactions. We present AdvGuard, a model-agnostic framework for detecting and mitigating system prompt leakage. AdvGuard models cross-query relationships using a bounded semantic interaction graph, statistically filters candidate components, and converts them into line graphs for graph convolutional network (GCN) classification. This approach captures multi-hop patterns in query similarity that distinguish coordinated extraction from benign workflows. A lightweight prompt-level detector provides protection before sufficient interaction history accumulates, and the framework supports black-box LLM deployments. In mixed-query evaluations, AdvGuard improves recall by up to 36% over the strongest baseline while maintaining a false positive rate of at most 3.4%. In multi-turn workloads, it achieves 97.23%-99.1% F1 with 100% recall. Leave-one-attack-family-out tests yield 99.98% mean recall and 99.99% mean F1, with no observed false positives. Integrated into the adaptive PLeak and LeakAgent attack loops, AdvGuard limits exact-match leakage to 0.00-0.01 and substring-match leakage to 0.01-0.09 across evaluated victim models. These results demonstrate robust detection of unseen attack families and substantially reduced prompt reconstruction.

items.title: Developing Critical AI Literacy Through Student-AI Dialogue in Engineering Education
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of artificial intelligence tools into higher education has created a critical paradox: students engage with AI daily yet rarely develop the skills to evaluate, question, or challenge AI-generated content. This paper presents the Cognitive Bridge methodology — a pedagogical framework developed and implemented at the National Polytechnic University of Armenia (NPUA) over nearly two years of iterative research and classroom practice (2024– 2026) — designed to transform AI from a passive answer-generator into an active cognitive challenge for engineering students. Grounded in Bloom's Revised Taxonomy and Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD), the methodology positions AI as a deliberately imperfect cognitive partner whose errors and limitations become the productive substance of learning. Over a four-week quasi-experimental intervention involving approximately 150 engineering students, participants progressed from intuitive AI use (Week 1 baseline) through guided error-detection and critical questioning (Weeks 2–3) to independent AI auditing (Week 4). Findings are supported by a parallel anonymous survey of N=149 engineering students on AI ethics awareness, revealing moderate AI literacy (Q10: M=3.29/5; Q11: M=3.34/5) alongside critically low knowledge of the EU AI Act (Q12: M=2.27/5). Qualitative thematic analysis identified three dominant themes: AI dependency as the primary ethical concern, university responsibility for structured instruction, and spontaneous student recognition of the Cognitive Bridge instruction in anonymous surveys. Results suggest that structured, longitudinal AI-challenge pedagogy significantly develops critical thinking, verification habits, and ethical awareness, offering a scalable, low-cost model applicable across diverse institutional contexts.

items.title: Development of an Adaptive Intelligent System Based on Artificial Intelligence for Supporting Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders
items.abstract: Relevance . Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) comprises a group of neurodevelopmental conditions requiring personalized approaches to developmental and educational support. Traditional approaches have limitations in terms of scalability and individualization. Objective . To analyze existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based solutions for supporting children with ASD and to describe the concept of a text-based intelligent system capable of dynamic learning and individualized adaptation. Methodology . Current AI-based solutions for supporting children with ASD were reviewed, including cognitive support platforms, conversational chatbots, robotic systems, and generative AI applications. An adaptive system architecture with a gamified interface was developed. Results . A concept for a text-based AI system was proposed that generates an individual child profile and adapts the difficulty, format, and content of tasks in real time. The system incorporates the principles of applied behavior analysis (ABA) and the Developmental, Individual-differences, Relationship-based (DIR)/Floortime approach at the level of its decision-making logic. Conclusion . The development of a text-based adaptive AI system represents a promising direction that combines advances in artificial intelligence with approaches to developmental and educational support.

items.title: Development of an Interactive Ground Monitoring Console and Telemetry Analytics Framework for General Aviation Flight Operations
items.abstract: Continuous monitoring of aircraft flight data is vital for proactive aviation safety, air traffic management, and predictive maintenance. Traditional Flight Data Recorders (FDR) store parameters on-board, limiting data accessibility to post-flight or post-accident investigations. This paper presents the development of an interactive Ground Monitoring Console (GMC) and telemetry analytics framework tailored for general aviation flight operations. Utilizing the high-fidelity CAFUC2 multi-model aviation benchmark dataset collected from Cessna 172R aircraft sorties, we process and validate multi-parameter telemetry streams including altitude (Mean = 3,800.4 ft, Std = 1,312.6 ft), vertical speed climb/descent distributions (3,129 climb vs 3,418 descent samples), pitch/roll attitudes (Mean = 2.55° and 1.35°), engine speed (Mean = 1,930.2 RPM, Std = 223.4 RPM), fuel flow (Mean = 8.23 GPH), and 2D GPS spatial navigation trajectories. A multi-panel software console is designed to integrate live spectrum monitoring, Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) constellation diagnostics (achieving 9.96% Error Vector Magnitude at 20 dB SNR), carrier signal quality indicators, and flight status displays. The framework provides ground controllers and flight safety officers with enhanced situational awareness and early warning capabilities without imposing heavy computational overhead. This foundational system establishes the baseline telemetry visualization architecture for future high-frequency RF front-ends.

items.title: Differentiating DeepSeek AI-generated translations from NMT translations and human translations within Chinese white paper discourse: a computer-based method for analyzing writing style
items.abstract: This study investigates whether distinct “machine-translationese” and “LLM-translationese” exist in Chinese–English government translation by comparing DeepSeek V4Pro, Google neural machine translation, and pre-neural human translation. We built the corpus as 24 minimally overlapping 5,000-word windows per translation condition, yielding 72 matched observations. Using 21 normalized linguistic features selected exclusively within a group-aware training partition, five classifiers were trained and evaluated with a fully held-out, chunk-disjoint test set, and their stability was cross-checked with nested cross-validation and 50 repeated group-aware splits. Naive Bayes and Random Forest emerged as the most consistently above-chance classifiers, while the remaining classifiers were weaker or more sensitive to the specific partition. This indicates that the three translation agents are distinguishable from linguistic form alone. A five-factor multidimensional analysis identified discourse cohesion and causal-deictic linking as the strongest and most stable group contrast separating human translation from both machine systems, alongside four additional, comparatively weaker dimensions capturing nominal/lexical density, nominalization and wh-subordination, lexical diversity and dynamic aspect, and elaborative/predicative complexity. Corrected pairwise comparisons confirmed that human translation exceeds both machine systems on discourse cohesion, and that Google NMT and DeepSeek V4Pro are statistically indistinguishable from one another on most dimensions. A chunk-level bootstrap analysis confirmed that, in five-dimensional factor space, DeepSeek V4Pro and Google NMT sit reliably closer to each other than either does to human translation, supporting a shared machine-translationese distinct from institutional human translation. The study documents differences in stylistic profile and presents the proposed links to reader cognitive load and RLHF-driven hedging as hypotheses emerging from these structural findings. These results provide an empirically grounded, methodologically conservative basis for discussing LLM- and NMT-based translation in official contexts.

items.title: Digest as Commitment, Not Blueprint: A Forward-Only Correction of the Digest-Reconstruction Narrative in SQUIRL OS Materials
items.abstract: Forward-only correction addendum to the SQUIRL OS research corpus. items.title: Digital Interventions for Identity Development: The Effects of Self-Reflection vs. AI-mediated Reflection on Exploration and Commitment Processes
items.abstract: As emerging adults (ages 18-30) figure out who they are and who they want to become, they often face the challenge of determining what career path to pursue. Many of them are also engaging with digital media, including conversational AI agents, while navigating these identity development processes. Although researchers recognize that identity develops in a digital context, little is known about how media can influence identity and its development. This study draws from past positive identity intervention research to better understand how digital media – and AI in particular — can be leveraged to support personal and vocational identity development. Here, we have developed and now aim to evaluate the efficacy of a digital intervention that consists of career-focused media prescriptions as treatments (i.e., AI reflection activities) that are designed to promote adaptive identity processes via reflection. We have recruited college students from the Bay Area into a randomized controlled trial to compare two active intervention conditions: (1) Self-Reflection (i.e., self-guided reflection activities) and (2) AI-mediated Reflection (i.e., AI chat reflection activities). The study design included between-person random assignment and within-person repeated measures collected before, during, and after the intervention. Our findings will show whether digital interventions incorporating reflection activities cause adaptive change in identity processes, while also demonstrating whether self-guided or AI-mediated reflection offers a promising approach for scaling developmental support for young people as they transition to adulthood.

items.title: Digital technologies and women artisan entrepreneurship: negotiating opportunities and constraints in conservative sociocultural contexts
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how women artisan entrepreneurs in northern Nigeria leverage digital technologies to pursue business opportunities and negotiate digital visibility within a conservative sociocultural context. This study also explores how digital entrepreneurship creates opportunities for market participation while remaining shaped by gendered social norms and constraints. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative case study approach based on semi-structured interviews with women artisan entrepreneurs operating in northern Nigeria. Findings The findings show how women artisans strategically use social media platforms, particularly Instagram and TikTok, to expand their market access, gain entrepreneurial knowledge, collaborate with peers and balance business with family responsibilities. However, they negotiate these opportunities within a conservative sociocultural environment that shapes their mobility, digital visibility and customer interactions, while also exposing them to online harassment and other gendered digital risks. Practical implications The study suggests that entrepreneurship support initiatives should move beyond improving digital access to strengthening women’s digital capabilities through training in social media marketing, customer relationship management, artificial intelligence and digital safety. Policies should also address gender-specific online risks through accessible reporting mechanisms and stronger platform-level trust and verification systems. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this study provides one of the first in-depth qualitative analyses of women artisan entrepreneurs’ use of digital technologies in northern Nigeria. It advances artisan entrepreneurship and cyberfeminism scholarship by showing how women strategically navigate digital opportunities and sociocultural constraints, offering a contextually grounded understanding of digital entrepreneurship.

items.title: Digital Transformation 2.0: Integrating AI and Empowering People for Sustainable Growth in the Future of Work
items.abstract: The digital era has reached a new inflection point, accelerated by artificial intelligence (AI) and organizations’ need to adapt to dynamic, technology-driven conditions. This chapter examines the legacy of Digital Transformation 1.0—highlighting failures and their causes—and defines the imperatives of AI-infused Digital Transformation 2.0. Drawing from relevant case studies, research, and executive interviews, it emphasizes the critical shift from episodic digitization to sustained AI-embedded digitalization. Leaders must enable systems-level transformation across people, process, and technology while aligning cultural, ethical, and operational domains. Digital Transformation 2.0 demands coordinated iterative design over monolithic strategy, requiring organizations to reimagine work as a fluid mix of tasks rather than fixed roles. Human–AI collaboration is a new reality that depends on psychological safety, AI literacy, and digital dexterity across the blended human-AI workforce. Successful transformation hinges on new leadership behaviors that elevate trust, agency, and adaptability while modeling and encouraging the use of new tools. The piece explores decentralized workforce models, the urgency of building AI-ready cultures, and a new social contract. It examines how agile frameworks, value mapping, and upskilling efforts create coherence amid complexity, making change tangible and participatory. The Future of Work is framed not as a fixed destination, but as a dynamic system requiring deliberate, ongoing leadership to combine machine capabilities with uniquely human capabilities. Ultimately, this work calls for defining or reframing organizational purpose and progress: AI can multiply what we value, but it is up to us to define what we value—and how we lead with it.

items.title: Digital Twin in Healthcare: A Review of Technologies, Applications and Challenges
items.abstract: A digital twin is a virtual replica of a physical entity that is continuously updated with real-world data and can be used to analyse, predict and test outcomes without risk to the original. Originally developed for aerospace and manufacturing, the concept is now being adapted to healthcare, where the twin may represent a single organ, an entire patient or a hospital. Conventional care relies on population averages, periodic check-ups and trial-and-error treatment, which leaves gaps in personalisation, early detection and safety. This paper reviews the concept of the healthcare digital twin, its enabling technologies (wearable sensors, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, medical imaging and health records, and 5G networks), a generic working architecture, and major application areas including personalised medicine, surgical planning, chronic disease management, drug development and hospital operations. It further discusses live patient monitoring, benefits, data privacy and regulatory considerations (HIPAA, GDPR and India’s DPDP Act 2023), and open challenges of cost, interoperability, workforce readiness and biological complexity. The review concludes that digital twins can make healthcare more predictive, personalised and safer, provided that privacy, standardisation and affordability are addressed.

items.title: DMAIC, Augmented: Generative AI Strengthens Lean Six Sigma Execution
items.abstract: This article examines how generative artificial intelligence (AI) assistants can strengthen Lean Six Sigma (LSS) execution across every phase of the Define-Measure-Analyze-Improve-Control (DMAIC) methodology. The objective is to give LSS practitioners field-tested patterns, quantified cycle-time data, and a governance framework for integrating AI assistants into quality-improvement projects without compromising methodological rigor. The investigation draws on recent industry deployments using Anthropic’s Claude assistant and a construct called skills: versioned playbooks that bundle written instructions, scripts, reference data, and validation rules into reusable artifacts. Methods include direct measurement of cycle-time deltas across Define, Measure, and Control tasks; four worked Analyze-phase examples spanning hypothesis testing, Measurement System Analysis, Statistical Process Control, and regression interpretation; and analysis of a multi-skill portfolio deployed at a small aviation services client. Results demonstrate substantial efficiency gains: project-charter drafting time fell from 90 to 120 minutes to roughly 6 minutes; monthly payroll consolidation fell from 90 minutes to under 30 seconds (a 99.4 percent reduction) with the first-pass error rate dropping to zero; cross-system benefits reconciliation fell from 4 hours to under 60 seconds, with monthly completion improving from 5 of 12 cycles to 12 of 12. The aggregate skills portfolio at one client achieved approximately 84 hours of administrative cycle-time savings per year. The article identifies six required governance controls (human review, version control, controlled prompts, sensitive-data boundaries, hallucination mitigation, and auditability) and aligns them with ISO 9001: 2015 and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. The conclusion is that generative AI does not alter DMAIC methodology; it lowers the cost of executing each phase well, expanding the share of LSS that is practiced in fact rather than only in theory. The findings support Master Black Belts and quality champions in deliberately piloting AI-enabled tooling, prioritizing Control-phase tasks first, and treating skill development as a formal deliverable with version control, ownership, and quality gates.

items.title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
items.abstract: Objective: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare has opened new possibilities for AI-assisted clinical decision-making; however, safe and effective deployment remains challenging because of hallucination and domain misalignment. This study introduces DocTalk, a doctor-assistive question-answering (QA) system designed to generate concise, chart-grounded responses from de-identified discharge summaries. Methods: We developed a high-fidelity data generation pipeline that produces 500 clinically relevant QA pairs through sentence-level decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question formulation, and expert review. Six open-source LLMs, including three general-purpose and three biomedical models, were evaluated before and after parameter-efficient instruction tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). The framework integrates prompt engineering, in-context learning, and medically aligned evaluation to support factual and interpretable responses. Results: On DocTalk-QA, instruction tuning produced consistent improvements across lexical, semantic, and clinical fidelity metrics. The best-performing tuned model, Llama-3-Med42-8B, achieved ROUGE-L = 0.40, BERTScore-F1 = 0.76, and UMLS-F1 = 0.49. To examine external generalization beyond the DocTalk-QA dataset, the two best-performing models, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-3-Med42-8B, were evaluated on PubMedQA before and after instruction tuning. Accuracy improved from 0.931 to 0.977 for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and from 0.935 to 0.943 for Llama-3-Med42-8B. Conclusion: DocTalk was deployed as a secure web-based platform for interactive EHR querying. These findings suggest that clinically grounded instruction tuning can improve medical QA performance and support practical clinical decision support.

items.title: Does low confidence drive reliance on AI, or does reliance erode confidence? A four-wave RI-CLPM study of chinese language and literature undergraduates
items.abstract: Generative AI tools are now routinely used by Chinese Language and Literature majors for tasks once considered the province of individual literary craft: drafting verse, shaping narrative prose, revising fiction. Two competing accounts describe what this means for students’ confidence in their own creative writing. A cognitive-offloading account holds that repeated reliance on AI displaces the mastery experiences through which writing self-efficacy is built, so reliance erodes confidence over time. A compensatory-use account holds the reverse: students whose confidence is already low turn to AI to avoid the discomfort of unassisted composition, so low confidence drives reliance. Cross-sectional and standard cross-lagged designs cannot separate these accounts because they confound stable between-person differences with genuine within-person change. We addressed this using a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) across four waves spanning one academic year among Chinese Language and Literature undergraduates ( N = 390 recruited; N = 387 analyzed under full-information maximum likelihood, of whom 298 supplied complete four-wave data). Generative AI writing reliance (GAWR) and literary creative writing self-efficacy (LCWSE) were assessed at each wave. The trait-level association between the two constructs was negative and could not be distinguished from zero ( r = −.342, Δχ²(1) = 2.26, p = .133). At the within-person level, declines in self-efficacy predicted subsequent increases in reliance (β = −.276, p < .001). The reverse path, from reliance to subsequent self-efficacy, was smaller and fell short of the conventional threshold (β = −.085, p = .072). We state explicitly that this second result is not interpretable as evidence against erosion: a Monte Carlo power analysis put this design's power to detect an effect of that magnitude at 53.2%, close to a coin flip, so the erosion pathway is undetermined in these data and this null supplies no basis for concluding that erosion does not operate. A direct comparison of the two cross-lagged paths favored compensation (Δχ²(1) = 8.83, p = .003; bootstrap 95% CI for the difference [.020, .218] across 5,000 resamples), with the qualification that this comparison sets an adequately powered estimate against an underpowered one and therefore describes what this design was able to detect. Compensation is the pathway this study establishes; whether reliance also erodes confidence over a longer horizon is an open question. We discuss implications for writing pedagogy in Chinese Language and Literature programs and for how underpowered null results should be interpreted in AI-in-education panel research.

items.title: DPE-Rec: Diversity-Preserving and Efficient Diffusion Language Model Recommendation for Bundle Construction
items.abstract: Generative bundle construction completes a partially observed bundle by generating its missing items from a large product catalog. Compared to autoregressive LLMs, diffusion LLM emerges as a natural fit for this unordered generation task. Their bidirectional attention provides an inductive bias better aligned with unordered bundle construction. Iterative denoising can reveal multiple tokens per step, potentially reducing inference latency. However, directly applying DLMs to this task presents two key challenges: 1 Despite its flexible reveal order, confidence-guided decoding tends to postpone semantic-fork decisions until refinement tokens constrain their choices, reducing bundle diversity. 2 Revealing more tokens per step can compromise recommendation quality, stifling the potential for faster inference. We introduce DPE-Rec, a diffusion framework for diversity preservation and efficient recommendation. DPE-Rec preserves diversity by introducing semantic-fork-aware GRPO, which prioritizes semantic-fork decisions via autoregressive rollouts. It improves efficiency through pseudo-trajectory distillation, which concentrates learning from the vast random corruption space onto the compact trajectory-induced subspace visited by high-quality decoding, unlocking reliable multi-token decoding. Together, these components enable diverse and accurate bundle construction with substantially fewer denoise steps. Experiments on multiple bundle construction benchmarks show that DPE-Rec improves recommendation performance by 63% on average, and its fast variant achieves 25.6$times$ faster inference on average than existing generative recommendation arts, with minimal loss in recommendation quality.

items.title: E0.5: From Reconstructive to Future-Predictive 3D Foundations for Robotic World-Action Modeling
items.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) offer a promising framework for embodied intelligence, yet mainstream approaches remain centered on video foundation models or vision-language models. Even when geometric features extracted by 3D models such as VGGT are incorporated, they are typically passed into a video model or VLM that serves as the primary backbone, leaving 3D geometry as an auxiliary input or prediction target rather than the native foundation for world modeling. We present E0.5, a geometry-native world-action model built directly on 3D foundation models. E0.5 introduces two key innovations. First, it adopts a 3D foundation model as the primary backbone, making 3D geometry the native representation for both world modeling and action prediction. Second, it explicitly predicts future 3D states together with actions, enabling the model to capture geometric world dynamics beyond action-only modeling or future video prediction. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 first demonstrate the effectiveness of E0.5 without embodied-data pretraining, achieving success rates of 89.90\% and 50.09\% under clean and randomized settings, respectively. Building on these results, we further pretrain E0.5 on more than 160k robot trajectories from AgiBotWorld-Beta, jointly learning robot actions and future geometry within the pretrained 3D foundation. This embodied pretraining improves mean real-world manipulation success rates by approximately 15 and 7 percentage points on AgileX Piper and Zerith H1, respectively. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of geometry-native foundations to acquire robot interaction knowledge and transfer it to physical manipulation. E0.5 embodies this geometry-native approach as a member of the VWA family of world-action models.

items.title: EDGE AI-BASED REAL-TIME BATTERY MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS: TECHNOLOGY TRENDS AND DESIGN FRAMEWORK
items.abstract: Battery management systems (BMSs) increasingly require low-latency, reliable, and intelligent processing capabilities to support the rapid expansion of electric vehicles and stationary energy storage systems. Conventional centralized and cloud-dependent BMS architectures can provide advanced analytics but may face limitations associated with communication latency, network dependence, data transmission overhead, and privacy. Edge artificial intelligence (Edge AI) provides an alternative approach by performing data processing and intelligent inference close to the battery system. This review examines major technology trends in real-time BMSs and proposes a reference design framework for Edge AI-based battery management. Recent developments in battery sensing, artificial intelligence-based state estimation, decentralized computing, lightweight machine learning, digital twins, communication, and cybersecurity are reviewed. Based on these trends, a layered framework is proposed in which battery sensors and embedded controllers acquire operating data, edge processors perform preprocessing and intelligent analysis, and cloud platforms provide long-term data management, model updating, and fleet-level analytics. The framework emphasizes local state estimation, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, secure edge-cloud communication, and optional digital-twin integration. The review indicates that Edge AI can reduce dependence on continuous cloud connectivity and enable faster decision-making, although practical deployment remains constrained by limited embedded resources, model complexity, cybersecurity risks, heterogeneous battery platforms, and interoperability issues. Future BMS development is expected to combine lightweight AI, adaptive edge-cloud collaboration, explainable decision support, digital twins, and security-by-design principles.

items.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui efektivitas penggunaan media counting box terhadap keterlibatan siswa dan hasil belajar matematika siswa kelas I SD. Pendekatan kuantitatif digunakan dengan desain pre-eksperimental one group pretest-posttest design, melibatkan 25 siswa kelas I SD. Uji normalitas Kolmogorov-Smirnov menghasilkan nilai signifikansi 0,210 (p > 0,05). Rata-rata nilai pretest adalah 58,4 dan posttest 88,2. Analisis N-Gain menghasilkan nilai rata-rata 0,72 berkategori Tinggi. Keterlibatan siswa mencapai rata-rata 88,6% (Sangat Tinggi) yang mencakup dimensi perilaku (92%), emosional (86%), dan kognitif (88%). Media counting box efektif mengubah konsep abstrak berhitung menjadi pengalaman manipulatif konkret yang sesuai tahap perkembangan kognitif operasional konkret siswa kelas I SD. abstract This study aims to examine the effectiveness of counting box media on student engagement and mathematics learning outcomes in Grade I elementary school. A quantitative approach was employed using a pre-experimental one group pretest-posttest design with 25 Grade I students as research subjects. Data were collected through pretest and posttest instruments, student engagement observation sheets, and questionnaires. The Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality test yielded a significance value of 0.210 (p > 0.05), confirming normally distributed data. The mean pretest score was 58.4, which increased to 88.2 on the posttest. N-Gain analysis produced a mean score of 0.72, classified as High, indicating significant improvement in learning outcomes. Student engagement reached an average of 88.6% (Very High), comprising behavioral engagement (92%), emotional engagement (86%), and cognitive engagement (88%). These findings demonstrate that counting box media is effective in transforming abstract arithmetic concepts into concrete manipulative experiences aligned with the operational concrete cognitive development stage of Grade I students.

items.title: Effect of guideline-assisted prompting on large language model performance in medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw–related endodontic decision-making
items.abstract: Clinical decision-making in patients receiving antiresorptive medications requires balancing tooth preservation against the risk of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ). This study compared the performance of ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek in MRONJ-related endodontic scenarios and evaluated the effect of guideline-assisted prompting using the 2022 American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons Position Paper. Eighteen fictional and standardized MRONJ-related endodontic clinical scenarios were developed based on the 2022 AAOMS Position Paper and current scientific evidence. Three contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek) were evaluated using a two-phase study design consisting of baseline and guideline-assisted assessments. In the second phase, the complete AAOMS Position Paper was provided before evaluation of the same scenarios. Two endodontic specialists independently scored the anonymized responses across five clinical decision-making domains using a six-point ordinal scale (0–5). The primary outcome was the mean of the five domain scores, yielding an overall clinical decision-making score ranging from 0 to 5. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using the initial ratings, and disagreements were resolved through consensus before analysis. Linear mixed models (LMMs) were used for the primary analyses, with cumulative link mixed models (CLMMs) performed as sensitivity analyses for the ordinal domain scores. Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons were performed where appropriate. At baseline, ChatGPT achieved a significantly higher mean overall score than Claude (4.68 ± 0.14 vs. 4.29 ± 0.38). Following guideline-assisted prompting, Claude’s mean score increased to 4.68 ± 0.28 (+ 0.39 points on the 0–5 scale), and the statistically significant difference between ChatGPT and Claude was no longer observed. DeepSeek consistently received lower overall scores than both models. A significant overall phase effect ( p < 0.001) and model-by-phase interaction ( p = 0.004) were identified. Domain-level CLMM sensitivity analyses generally supported the LMM findings, although the phase effect for consultation and medication management was not confirmed by the CLMM. The most pronounced model-specific increase in guideline-concordant scores was observed for follow-up recommendations, particularly for Claude. Guideline-assisted prompting was associated with higher concordance with the predefined reference standard, particularly for Claude, which showed the largest improvement in overall scores and follow-up recommendations. Although ChatGPT scored significantly higher than Claude at baseline, this difference was no longer statistically significant following guideline-assisted prompting. Because the clinical scenarios, reference standard, and guideline-assisted intervention were aligned with the same AAOMS guideline, these findings should not be interpreted as independent validation of clinical accuracy. Further studies using externally developed scenarios and real-world clinical cases are required before considering these models for clinician-supervised decision support.

items.title: Effective Classification of Skin Related Diseases Using Medical Image Processing and Deep Learning Based Framework
items.abstract: Skin cancer ranks among mostly prevalent cancer types across the globe, and its treatment outcomes and survival rates show improvement through early detection methods which achieve precise results. The traditional methods of diagnosis depend on visual assessment and clinical expertise, which creates a risk of delayed detection and erroneous diagnosis. Using a specially selected dataset, this study suggests an effective deep learning-based method with data augmentation for the separation of skin cancer disorders in order to overcome these difficulties. Regarding the categorization of skin lesions into different groups, we have used CNN in conjunction with transfer learning models like VGG16 and VGG19. A balanced, specially created dataset of annotated skin lesion photos was used to train and evaluate the models. To increase generalization and model resilience, preprocessing methods and data augmentation were used. With a classification accuracy of up to 97% suggested system shows promising outcomes for high-precision faster medical diagnosis. Additionally, a comparative analysis of various models was carried out, emphasizing of trade-offs among training complexity, accuracy, computational efficiency. The potential of deep learning to provide dermatologists and other medical practitioners with automated, dependable, and scalable skin cancer detection systems is demonstrated through this study. Also Multimodal LLM Based Model is used for classification of diseases more accurately.

items.title: Ein Semesterkurs zur Förderung der wissenschaftlichen Informationskompetenz in den Biowissenschaften
items.abstract: An der BiblioCon 2026 in Berlin stellten wir unsere ganzsemestrige Lehrveranstaltung „Scientific Information Literacy“ vor, die von der Universitätsbibliothek Zürich für Studierende der Biowissenschaften angeboten wird. Dieser jährlich wiederkehrende Kurs vermittelt zentrale Kompetenzen der wissenschaftlichen Informationskompetenz, greift aktuelle Entwicklungen wie generative KI auf und kombiniert unterschiedliche Lehr- und Prüfungsformate. Am Beispiel des Kurses wird gezeigt, wie Liaison Librarianship dazu beitragen kann, bibliothekarische Lehrangebote gemeinsam mit den Fakultäten weiterzuentwickeln und langfristig in Studienprogramme einzubetten.At the BiblioCon 2026 in Berlin, we presented “Scientific Information Literacy”, a semester-long course offered by the University Library Zurich for students in the life sciences. This annual course teaches key concepts of scientific information literacy, addresses current developments such as generative artificial intelligence, and combines a variety of teaching and assessment formats. Using this course as an example, we suggest that liaison librarianship can contribute to the development of library-led educational offerings in close collaboration with the faculties of the university and support their long-term integration into curricula.

items.title: Emerging technologies as educational tools in cardiovascular health: empowering patients and training professionals
items.abstract: Health education has emerged as an essential component in the management of cardiovascular disease (CVD), especially in contexts where physical access to medical care may be limited. This study, conducted in Ibagué, Colombia, evaluated the role of emerging technologies in improving education for both patients and health professionals. Through expert interviews, technology watch, and the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), five technologies were prioritized for institutional implementation in cardiovascular care; their educational potential for patients and healthcare professionals was then analyzed as a complementary dimension. The results highlighted the educational impact of 3D model-ling, telemedicine, and artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical triage and in teaching complex cardiac conditions. The findings suggest that 3D modelling and printing, telemedicine, remote monitoring, and AI-supported tools have relevant educational potential in cardiovascular care. In particular, 3D-printed cardiac models may help improve patient understanding of complex conditions and may contribute to reducing uncertainty and supporting treatment adherence. Telemedicine and remote monitoring may facilitate autonomous learning, self-care, and patient empowerment, while AI applied to electrocardiogram analysis may support professional training through automated feedback and decision-support processes. In conclusion, the strategic integration of emerging technologies could strengthen cardiovascular education, support clinical communication, and contribute to better-informed care processes, provided that these tools are implemented with adequate infrastructure, professional training, and patient-centred educational strategies.

items.title: Emerging Trends in Global Banking and Investment Operations
items.abstract: Global banking and investment operations are changing as financial institutions adopt new technologies, expand into international markets, and strengthen risk management. Banks and investment firms must process transactions accurately, protect financial data, meet regulatory requirements, and deliver reliable services to clients across different regions. These changes are creating new expectations for banking operations professionals. In addition to financial knowledge, employers increasingly need people who understand data analysis, digital tools, compliance procedures, and process improvement. Automation is also changing routine tasks, which increases the value of skills in exception handling, analytical thinking, and operational control. India has become an important centre for global financial services and technology-enabled business operations. Hyderabad and Bengaluru are key locations in this ecosystem, with companies supporting financial processes, technology development, risk management, and business services. The changing landscape of global banking operations Global banking operations include the processes that support financial transactions across markets. These processes help financial institutions record trades, transfer funds and securities, maintain accurate data, and meet regulatory obligations. Operations teams work with front-office, middle-office, compliance, finance, and technology departments. Their responsibilities may include trade confirmation, settlement support, reconciliation, corporate actions, transaction monitoring, and financial reporting. Several forces are changing this work: The growth of cross-border transactions and international financial services. Greater use of automation and artificial intelligence. Increased focus on data quality and operational efficiency. Stronger requirements for risk management and regulatory compliance. Expansion of Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India. Rising demand for digital and analytical skills. These developments mean that banking operations are no longer limited to routine transaction processing. Many teams now support analysis, control monitoring, technology adoption, and process improvement. Artificial intelligence and intelligent automation Artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the main forces changing financial operations. Banks can use AI-based tools to review documents, classify information, detect unusual transaction patterns, and support customer service. Robotic process automation can also handle repetitive, rule-based tasks. The shift is moving from small pilot projects towards wider use across business functions. An EY India GCC Pulse Survey published in November 2025 reported that 58% of surveyed Indian GCCs were investing in agentic AI, while 83% were investing in generative AI. The survey also found that 81% were upskilling internal teams in generative AI. These findings indicate growing interest in both technology adoption and workforce development. For banking operations, automation can reduce manual data entry and support faster processing. However, automated systems still require oversight. Professionals must review exceptions, check outputs, identify errors, and follow approved controls. This creates a need for skills in process analysis, data validation, workflow monitoring, and risk awareness. Learners considering Certification In Global & Investment Banking Operations (CGIBO) in Hyderabad should look for opportunities to understand how modern banking processes use technology while maintaining accuracy and control. Data analytics and real-time financial reporting Financial institutions generate large amounts of data through payments, securities transactions, customer activity, and regulatory reporting. Data analytics helps operations teams turn this information into useful insights. Instead of relying only on manual checks, teams can use dashboards and analytical tools to monitor transaction volumes, identify processing delays, and detect recurring errors. This can help managers improve workflows and allocate resources more effectively. Important developments in this area include: Real-time monitoring: Tracking transactions and operational performance as events occur. Predictive analytics: Using historical data to identify possible risks and processing problems. Automated reporting: Reducing repetitive work and improving consistency. Data quality management: Checking records for missing, incorrect, or inconsistent information. Business intelligence: Presenting operational results through reports and dashboards. These capabilities are useful across trade support, reconciliation, risk operations, and financial reporting. Professionals who understand financial processes and can interpret data may be better prepared for roles that require both operational knowledge and analytical thinking. Learners researching Certification In Global & Investment Banking Operations (CGIBO) in Bangalore can review the programme curriculum to determine whether it covers relevant financial concepts, reporting processes, and practical applications. Stronger compliance and financial crime prevention Regulatory compliance remains a major priority for banks and investment firms. Financial institutions must follow applicable laws, protect customer information, maintain accurate records, and monitor transactions for suspicious activity. Know Your Customer (KYC), Anti-Money Laundering (AML), customer due diligence, sanctions screening, and fraud prevention are important parts of this work. A report published by the India Brand Equity Foundation in July 2025, citing Careernet research, stated that India's financial crime talent pool had grown to more than 25,500 professionals. The report identified Bengaluru as the largest centre in this talent pool, accounting for 32%, while Hyderabad accounted for 17%. It also highlighted demand across customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, fraud control, and regulatory compliance. These figures reflect the importance of specialised compliance skills in India's financial services ecosystem. They do not guarantee that vacancies will be available to every candidate, but they indicate areas worth monitoring when planning a career. Technology is also changing compliance work. items.title: End-to-End MXFP8 Reinforcement Learning on Blackwell: What Matching Buys, When It Pays Off, and How It Fails
items.abstract: Low-precision arithmetic can make reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models cheaper, but RL requires the sampler and the learner to agree. Several frameworks now run FP8 on both sides. We implement end-to-end MXFP8 RL in verl (Megatron/Transformer Engine training; vLLM and SGLang rollout; dense and MoE models) and measure on B200 GPUs, with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, what this design buys, when it is faster, and how it fails. (1) Matching. For an MXFP8 learner, a sampler on the learner's grid is more consistent than a higher-precision BF16 sampler: in one engine at fixed weights, train-rollout KL is 11% lower with half of the sampler's linear layers on the grid and 16% lower with all of them, and the synchronized weights we checked equal the learner's FP8 forward weights byte for byte. On the MoE model, an FP8 pipeline whose sampler uses another grid has twice the shared-grid pipeline's KL from the first step. Without a quantized KV cache, BF16 end to end remains 2.5-10x more consistent. (2) Speed. MXFP8 training adds a fixed cost per micro-batch and saves a per-token cost, so in our dense setting it pays off only above about 4.5k tokens per micro-batch; a micro-batch sweep on identical data confirms the per-micro-batch cost, and a trace shows the GPU waiting for the host for most of the added time. End to end, MXFP8 cuts MoE step time by 10.7% and generation time by 24%, and slows a short-sequence dense workload by 5%. (3) Correctness. We state seven conditions every weight synchronization must preserve and checks that test them against the live engine. Each of the seven failures we met on hardware broke one condition, five silently; the checks caught two at their first opportunity, each missed by the other checks, and CPU fault-injection tests reproduce five. All runs are single-seed and at most 60 steps long; we make no claim about final model quality.

items.title: Energy access, global integration, human development, and institutional complementarity for artificial intelligence development in Africa
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence is a key driver of economic growth and sustainable development for modern economies. Its development relies heavily on enabling conditions such as access to electricity, globalization, openness, effective regulatory quality, and skilled human capital. This study examined the dynamic relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI) and energy access, as well as the impact of globalization, human development, regulatory quality, and globalization policy on AI development in Africa. It covered 2015 to 2023 and used the System Generalized Method of Moments. Employing panel data, it adopted a reverse approach to existing studies to examine the impact of energy poverty on AI and determined the moderating effect of regulatory quality, globalization policy, and energy poverty on AI adoption. Its main objective is to examine the dynamic influence of energy poverty on Artificial Intelligence in Africa and contribute evidence relevant to the UN Sustainable Development Goals 7 and 9. Findings show that energy access significantly undermines Artificial Intelligence development. It further revealed that globalization and human development are negative and insignificant determinants of AI development, while regulatory quality exhibits a marginally significant ( p -value = 0.057) support for AI development. Further findings reveal that the synergistic interaction between energy access and globalization policy significantly reduced the impact of energy access on AI development. Meanwhile, the marginal negative effect of the interaction between energy access and regulatory quality on AI development is insignificant. The study recommends the prioritization of affordable and reliable energy, a shift from general to strategic globalization, AI skill-related development programs, quality institutions, effective integration policies , and enabling conditions to improve AI in Africa.

items.title: Engaging Every Student: Applying Theories of Motivation in Physical Education to Foster Student Involvement
items.abstract: Motivating students has long been a challenge for physical educators, a problem exacerbated by declining physical activity rates among school-age youth. As physical education is often a child’s first structured exposure to physical activity, effective instruction that intrinsically motivates youth is crucial for cultivating healthy and active lifestyles. Student motivation in physical education can be understood as the direction and intensity of participation, influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors frequently determined by teacher actions. Extrinsic motivators often fall short of building long-term commitment from students, while lasting engagement in physical activity, both inside and outside of the gymnasium, stems from students’ intrinsic motivation to participate. Effective physical education teachers must be intentional in selecting and utilizing pedagogical strategies that not only motivate students to learn but also encourage them to develop their own intrinsic motivation for lifelong physical activity. This article discusses motivational theories and their role in creating an environment that inspires students to perform, persist, and grow. It presents popular theories of motivation relevant to physical education, along with applied pedagogical strategies aligned with each theory to support the development of intrinsically motivated students.

items.title: Enhancing 6G Positioning Accuracy through AI-Driven Localization Algorithms
items.abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks target ultra-high data rates, sub-millisecond latencies, and centimeterto-millimeter-level positioning accuracy. This unprecedented localization precision is essential for missioncritical applications such as autonomous transportation, smart grids, extended reality (XR), and industrial automation. However, operating at high frequencies (millimeter-wave and Terahertz bands) exposes 6G signals to severities including rapid path loss, signal blockages, and complex multipath interference. Traditional geometric and range-based methods face fundamental performance ceilings under these non-line-of-sight (NLoS) and dynamic channel conditions. This paper proposes a hybrid, artificial intelligence-assisted localization framework to solve these challenges. We design a multi-layer feedforward backpropagation Artificial Neural Network (ANN) trained on multi-path Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) profiles. To tackle high-velocity user equipment (UE) tracking in dense urban centers, we deploy a self-tuning Kalman Filter (KF) configured directly over the raw neural network predictions. We evaluate our design in a simulated100m equilateral 6G base station grid. Under dynamic shadowing conditions (1.5 dB) and high velocity (35 m/s or 126 km/h), the proposed hybrid model successfully reduces the mean physical positioning error from 7.970 meters (baseline static ANN) to 4.380 meters—achieving a substantial 45.04% improvement in tracking accuracy and a 41.83% improvement in the 90th percentile bounds (down to 7.793 meters). These empirical results validate the robustness of blending low-overhead AI models with temporal kinetic filters, supporting high-fidelity location services in next-generation networks.

items.title: Enhancing Students Speaking Skills Through Small Group Discussion Supported by ChatGPT Voice at SMPN 4 Koto Baru
items.abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of Small Group Discussion supported by ChatGPT Voice on student’s speaking skills at SMPN 4 Koto Baru. A quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was employed. The participants considered of 27 seventh-grade A student’s selected through total sampling. Data were collected using speaking tests assessing pronunciation, fluency, vocabulary, and grammar. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, and Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test. The results showed that the students mean score increased from 34.81 in the pre-test and 44.44 in the post-test. The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test yielded a significance value of 0.000 (p < 0.05). Therefore, the null hypothesis (H0) was rejected, and the alternative hypothesis (Ha) was accepted. Indicating that Small Group Discussion supported by ChatGPT Voice has a significant positive effect on students speaking skills. These findings suggest that integrating collaborative learning with AI-assisted speaking practice can serve as an effective strategy for improving students speaking skills.

items.title: Enhancing transport innovation knowledge management workflows using artificial intelligence: a TRIMIS database case study
items.abstract: Abstract The Transport Research and Innovation Monitoring and Information System (TRIMIS) tracks EU-funded transport research and innovation projects to identify trends and inform policymaking. A key function of TRIMIS is maintaining a comprehensive and accurate database of transport projects. Selecting and categorising relevant projects is a manual and time-consuming process. This study explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI), specifically large language models (LLMs), to support and accelerate this task. A workflow was developed using an LLM platform (GENESIS, the JRC internal, secure, general-purpose LLM platform), iteratively refining prompts to match expert human judgment in identifying relevant projects from CORDIS. Comparing LLM-generated outputs to the existing TRIMIS database, projects were assessed for inclusion/exclusion and classified by transport mode and sector, and technology thematic area. The classifications allow for filtering and consequent analysis and visualisation by these categories. A further application investigated was the assessment of projects for their contribution to the competitiveness of the EU Automotive Industry. Prompt engineering iterations and structured output analysis improved accuracy and consistency and reduced the risk of unsupported or fabricated classifications by requiring every positive decision to be grounded in a verbatim quotation from the project text. Using the ensemble configuration, we analysed 52,923 Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe projects (2014–2026), identifying 6,986 relevant for inclusion in the TRIMIS database, with reporting in this paper focused on the most recent 19,025 Horizon Europe projects, of which 2,184 (11.5%) were assessed as relevant. The analysis of the full corpus required about two days of serial model time for the two deployed configurations (Annex 5), reducing manual work and identifying matches in previously overlooked funding sources. Outcomes also helped to re-evaluate existing taxonomies. The results demonstrate the potential of AI-assisted workflows to reduce manual workload, improve accuracy, and scale project curation for the TRIMIS database, with broader implications for using AI-assisted methods in public-sector knowledge management. Future work will explore hybrid human-AI review pipelines and domain-specific fine-tuning.

VOCATIONAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL EDUCATION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: CHALLENGES AND POSSIBILITIES FOR PROFESSIONAL TRAINING IN THE DIGITAL AGE. EDUCACIÓN PROFESIONAL Y TECNOLÓGICA E INTELIGENCIA ARTIFICIAL: DESAFÍOS Y POSIBILIDADES PARA LA FORMACIÓN DE PROFESIONALES EN LA ERA DIGITAL. Gabriel Nascimento de Carvalho Simone Helen Drumond Ischkanian Gladys Nogueira Cabral Celine Maria de Sousa Azevedo Silvana Nascimento de Carvalho Sygride Nascimento de Carvalho Sandro Garabed Ischkanian RESUMO A Educação Profissional e Tecnológica (EPT) enfrenta desafios relacionados à incorporação da inteligência artificial nos processos de ensino e aprendizagem, na organização curricular e no desenvolvimento de competências necessárias ao mundo do trabalho. A expansão das tecnologias digitais demanda reflexões sobre as possibilidades de inovação pedagógica, a preparação dos docentes, a formação crítica dos estudantes e as implicações éticas do uso de sistemas inteligentes. Diante desse cenário, estabelece-se como problema de pesquisa: de que maneira a inteligência artificial pode contribuir para a formação de profissionais na EPT, considerando as exigências da transformação digital e os desafios de sua implementação educacional? O objetivo geral consiste em analisar os desafios e as possibilidades da integração da inteligência artificial à formação profissional, com atenção às competências técnicas, digitais, críticas e éticas requeridas na contemporaneidade. Metodologicamente, propõe-se uma pesquisa qualitativa, de caráter exploratório e descritivo, desenvolvida por meio de revisão bibliográfica e análise documental de publicações científicas e documentos institucionais pertinentes à temática. A análise permite discutir possibilidades de personalização da aprendizagem, apoio às atividades pedagógicas, simulação de situações profissionais e aproximação entre educação e transformações tecnológicas. Também evidencia desafios relativos à infraestrutura, à formação docente, à proteção de dados, aos vieses algorítmicos e às desigualdades de acesso. Conclui-se que a integração da inteligência artificial à EPT requer planejamento pedagógico, formação continuada e princípios éticos, de modo a articular inovação tecnológica, inclusão educacional e desenvolvimento humano na preparação dos profissionais para a era digital. ABSTRACT Professional and Technological Education (PTE) faces challenges related to the incorporation of artificial intelligence into teaching and learning processes, curriculum organization, and the development of skills required in the world of work. The expansion of digital technologies calls for reflection on the possibilities of pedagogical innovation, teacher preparation, students’ critical development, and the ethical implications of using intelligent systems. Against this background, the research problem is formulated as follows: how can artificial intelligence contribute to professional training in PTE, considering the demands of digital transformation and the challenges of its educational implementation? The general objective is to analyze the challenges and possibilities of integrating artificial intelligence into professional education, focusing on the technical, digital, critical, and ethical competencies required in contemporary society. Methodologically, the study adopts a qualitative, exploratory, and descriptive approach, based on a literature review and documentary analysis of scientific publications and institutional documents relevant to the topic. The analysis discusses opportunities for personalized learning, support for pedagogical activities, simulation of professional situations, and closer alignment between education and technological change. It also identifies challenges involving infrastructure, teacher training, data protection, algorithmic bias, and unequal access. The study concludes that integrating artificial intelligence into PTE requires pedagogical planning, continuing professional development, and ethical principles to connect technological innovation, educational inclusion, and human development in preparing professionals for the digital age. items.title: Ergonomic Workload, Musculoskeletal Symptoms, and Physiological Strain Among Juvenile Female Brickfield Workers: A Field-Based Analytical Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract: Background: Juvenile (adolescent) girls from socio-economically disadvantaged households continue to perform heavy manual material-handling (MMH) tasks in India’s unorganized brick-manufacturing sector, despite legal protections against child labour. Evidence on their ergonomic exposures, physiological strain, and musculoskeletal health remains scarce. Objective: To evaluate the physical workload, postural stress, thermal exposure, musculoskeletal symptom prevalence, and acute physiological responses of juvenile girls employed in manual brick manufacturing units in West Bengal, India. Methods: A cross-sectional study design was adopted involving 100 young females within the age group of 13 to 18 years who worked at brick manufacturing plants in Nadia and Howrah districts of West Bengal. Data collection included interviews using modified Nordic questionnaires, anthropometry, activity observations both direct and video recorded, postural analysis through the Ovako Working Posture Analysis System (OWAS), thermal environment assessment, and physiological parameters both pre and post tasks of brick carrying. A paired t-test was performed to assess the physiological parameters before and after brick carrying, while the chi-square test was used to determine any relationship between musculoskeletal symptoms and BMI or the number of bricks handled per day. Results: The mean age was 15.5±2.33 years, BMI was 18.90±1.52 kg/m² and the occupational experience was 1.3±0.6 years. In general, 91% of participants complained of job-related pain, including the head (72%), neck (72%), and leg (78%). Neck pain was statistically correlated with chronic energy deficiencies (BMI < 18.5 kg/m², χ² = 9.675, p = 0.0019). Lifting more than 2,000 bricks per day was statistically correlated with head pain (χ² = 6.722, p = 0.0095), neck pain (χ² = 4.228, p = 0.0397), shoulder pain (χ² = 4.396, p = 0.0360), and back pain (χ² = 10.306, p = 0.0013). Bricks lifting led to a significant increase in heart rate (from 80.33±3.67 to 112.45±2.13 beats/min, p < 0.05), systolic blood pressure (from 119.7±3.5 to 134.9±5.15 mmHg, p < 0.05), and perceived exertion level (from 13.2±1.5 to 18.6±0.45). Participants performed 45% of the tasks moderately and 25% heavily; unloading bricks from the kiln top was the most dangerous according to the OWAS scale. Conclusion: Manual brick production entails heavy postural, thermal, and cardiovascular stress along with extremely high levels of musculoskeletal symptoms in female juveniles. There is an urgent need for intervention measures regarding ergonomics, nutrition, regulation, and education, including the abolition of hazardous juvenile labor, mechanization of load carrying, load restriction, rest breaks, hydration, safe postures, and schooling.

items.title: Ethical boundaries for the use of artificial intelligence in academic assessment
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine educators’ perceptions of the ethical boundaries for using artificial intelligence (AI) in teaching and academic assessment, distinguishing AI support from AI delegation using flipped learning as a pedagogical lens. Design/methodology/approach A questionnaire was administered to 148 faculty members from Universidade Autónoma de Lisboa, Portugal. The paper adopts an exploratory quantitative case-study design. Analysis used descriptive statistics, normalized Shannon entropy, Pearson correlation and a paired-samples t-test. Findings Respondents were open to AI support for routine, preparatory and lower-order learning activities, but more cautious when AI was associated with evaluation, fairness, interpretation and assessment decisions. Teacher judgment was strongly prioritized, while trust in AI-generated fair and unbiased evaluation remained limited. Entropy analysis showed relatively clear boundaries around AI bias and human judgment, but more contested boundaries around AI-supported evaluation, learner independence and critical reflection. Research limitations/implications The single-institution convenience sample should be interpreted as exploratory and analytically transferable rather than statistically generalizable. Practical implications Institutions should clarify where AI may support assessment and where human evaluative authority must remain explicit. Social implications The findings highlight the need for shared institutional norms. Originality/value The paper proposes the dual approach as an interpretive framework connecting ethical responsibility, cognitive complexity and flipped learning to distinguish AI support from delegated evaluative authority. Its contribution lies in locating the ethical boundary at the transfer of assessment responsibility and identifying where educators’ perceptions indicate crisp or fuzzy boundaries.

items.title: Ethical, Legal, and Regulatory Challenges in Modern Healthcare
items.abstract: It is assumed that the synergies created by the 6G communication technologies, blockchain organizations, and smart healthcare systems will introduce Society 5.0 in the form of the hyper-connected and patient-centric secure health ecosystem. These technologies are expected to provide an opportunity of unprecedented socio-economic value by real-time remote health monitoring and interaction, decentralized patient data management systems, and clinical decision making based on artificial intelligence. It is not only an ethical and societal but also a legal and regulatory challenge. Patient privacy, ownership of data, bias in the algorithm, and cyber security will have to be taken into consideration before we go into full deployment. Also, there exists no unified legal framework, as well as there are cross-border regulations to back a blockchain empowered contributor-led 6G healthcare system. The chapter will discuss ethical implications, legal issues, and regulations involved with 6G and blockchain-enabled health care and answer the question of what patients should think about informed consent when offered AI-led care, liability when making independent choices, and what the compliance with the right of the citizens to privacy under the jurisdiction of their nation (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA), and what regulatory models might be available to decentralized health systems. We finally make high level recommendation concerning future policies and regulation to strike a balance between innovation, patient safety and social trust by the people.

items.title: Ethics by Configuration: AI Ethics Principles in Coding Agent Instructions
items.abstract: As AI coding agents become integral to software development, projects increasingly utilise configuration files, such as context files and skills, to govern agent behaviour. While AI ethics principles are widely used in research and policy, little is known about whether and how they are reflected when developers configure coding agents. We studied ethics principles in 40,079 configuration files across 8,893 GitHub repositories. Using a validated large language model (LLM) classification, we measured the prevalence of ethics-related statements, and qualitatively analysed 702 stratified samples across 679 files to uncover the ethical considerations reflected in these files and the parties they concern. Ethics-related statements appeared in 39.4% of files and 61.5% of repositories; concentrated on accountability, transparency, privacy protection, and reliability; and occurred more often in task-specific files such as skills than in project-wide context files. Our qualitative analysis identified 30 categories of ethical considerations, which take the form of concrete rules for the agent. Accountability appeared mainly as requirements for human approval, transparency as explain and honestly report the agent's work, and fairness as accessibility and localisation. These considerations reveal a difference in focus. Whereas public ethics frameworks aim to protect society and end users, configuration files mainly concern developers, maintainers, and community members in the development workflow. Ethics-related content appeared mainly in prose-based files, and whether agents follow these instructions remains untested. We discuss the implications for practitioners, researchers, and policymakers.

items.title: Evaluating an LLM-assisted workflow for clinical documentation: A pilot randomized controlled trial on time and quality
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been investigated for clinical documentation, with concerns about hallucinations and factual errors. Clinician review and revision of LLM-generated drafts are considered essential; however, the impact of such a workflow on both documentation time and quality remains unknown. This single-center, parallel-group, prospective, randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint (PROBE) pilot trial evaluated whether a clinician-in-the-loop workflow improves clinical documentation time and quality compared with clinician-only drafting. From February 18 to March 14, 2025, at the Department of Ophthalmology, Kyoto University Hospital, 21 physicians were randomized, and 17 completed the intervention. Participants were randomized to either the Clinician-in-the-loop group or the Clinician-only group. Participants created discharge summaries and referrals for six simulated patient records. The Clinician-in-the-loop group reviewed and edited LLM-generated drafts, whereas the Clinician-only group drafted documents from scratch using matched templates. Unedited LLM drafts formed the LLM-only group. Seventeen physicians submitted 48 discharge summaries and 48 discharge referrals in the Clinician-in-the-loop group, 54 of each document type in the Clinician-only group, and 48 of each in the LLM-only group. Clinician-in-the-loop showed a shorter creation time for summaries (β = −59.4 seconds; 95% CI, −150.6 to 31.7; P = .18) and a longer creation time for referrals (β = 52.9 seconds; 95% CI, −7.0 to 112.9; P = .08) than Clinician-only, although neither difference was statistically significant. In most expert-rated quality domains, the clinician-in-the-loop workflow outperformed clinician-only drafting. LLM-only drafts were fastest but had the lowest quality. In conclusion, a clinician-in-the-loop approach generally improved document quality and, although the primary analysis showed no statistically significant difference in documentation time, suggested potential time savings for certain document types. These findings highlight the importance of active clinician supervision and support further evaluation of clinician-in-the-loop workflows in real-world clinical settings. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT07187050 (registered on September 18, 2025).

items.title: Evaluating Federated Vision-Language and Vision-Only Models for Privacy-Aware Breast Cancer Imaging
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise for breast imaging, but limited labeled data, institutional data fragmentation, and privacy concerns hinder centralized training. We investigate a privacy-aware federated learning framework combining pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) with client-level differential privacy. We compare general-purpose CLIP models, biomedical BiomedCLIP, and an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B/16 baseline on two public breast imaging datasets, with and without differential privacy. We also evaluate a CLIP ViT-B/16 ablation that removes the text pathway. Evaluation includes patient-level ROC-AUC with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, baseline comparisons, threshold sensitivity, inter-model agreement, and communication cost. Under federated learning, all five models achieve high normal-versus-sick discrimination (ROC-AUC: 0.940-0.990). However, acquisition year alone achieves 0.974 on the same test partition, raising concerns about confounding rather than genuine pathology recognition. Benign-versus-malignant discrimination remains uncertain (ROC-AUC: 0.504-0.637), with all confidence intervals including 0.50. Removing the text pathway preserves classification accuracy while halving communication cost. Differential privacy reduces ROC-AUC by 0.375, attributable to perturbing the full model state rather than only trainable parameters. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating confounding, predictive reliability, privacy implementation, and deployment efficiency when developing federated AI systems for breast imaging.

items.title: Evaluating Foundation Time-Series Models in Systematic Options Compounding
items.abstract: A prevailing belief in quantitative finance is that deploying high-capacity foundation models inevitably generates superior predictive edge (Gu, Kelly, & Xiu, 2020). This paper presents an empirical evaluation testing whether zero-shot foundation forecasting (Google TimesFM 1.0-200M; Das, Kong, Sen, & Zhou, 2024) and kinematic derivatives physics enhance strike selection and compounding in systematic options selling across Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOG), and NVIDIA (NVDA) over a continuous 10-year cycle (October 2016 to October 2026 | 2,512 trading days), strictly partitioned into a 5-year In-Sample calibration epoch and a 5-year Out-of-Sample holdout period. We simulate mechanical options compounding under an idealized Zero-VRP invariant (pricing all contracts at zero implied-volatility premium via analytical Black-Scholes-Merton) to isolate pure directional and timing alpha from structural volatility premium capture. On this invariant benchmark, baseline rule-based mechanics achieve terminal equity of $2,349,600 on AMZN (23.50x), $821,300 on GOOG (8.21x), and $27,998,700 on NVDA (280.0x). Integrating TimesFM 10-day ahead forecasts to write defensive call overlays produces zero statistically detectable forecast edge: directional accuracy is indistinguishable from coin flips (50.8% AMZN, 51.2% GOOG, 49.8% NVDA; Diebold-Mariano p-values 0.27, 0.11, 0.42), while call truncation inflicts catastrophic opportunity cost on explosive trend legs (NVDA terminal wealth collapses from 280.0x to 10.9x). Furthermore, kinematic dip-buying rules (velocity-acceleration phase triggers) display severe parameter decay out of sample: on AMZN, out-of-sample terminal wealth sits at the 72.4th percentile of an uninformed random-put placebo (p = 0.28). Deflated Sharpe Ratios (DSR; Bailey & Lopez de Prado, 2014) across all evaluated machine learning enhancements fall to 0.00, demonstrating that the observed historical outperformance was a product of selection bias across non-stationary market regimes.

items.title: Evaluating Predictive World-Model Representations for Long-Horizon Forklift–Worker Risk Forecasting
items.abstract: Predictive world models can simulate plausible future physical scenes, but their value as frozen representations for specialized industrial safety tasks remains unclear. We examine whether predictive future latents from NVIDIA Cosmos Predict2.5 2B add sample-specific information beyond a compact kinematic history for long-horizon forklift–worker risk forecasting. From a 2 s state history, the task predicts both agents’ positions, their cumulative minimum separation, and HIGH/WARNING/SAFE risk from +1 to +6 s. Using 1180 samples from 854 synthetic warehouse runs, a state-only predictor is compared with a residual fusion of aligned Cosmos latents, the same residual with shuffled latents, and a Cosmos-only model. On 300 test samples from 129 runs, the state-only model achieves a worker average displacement error of 0.484 m and a mean risk Macro-F1 of 0.846; the aligned residual yields 0.496 m and 0.845, and the shuffled control 0.485 m and 0.850. Run-level cluster bootstrap analysis and ten strict shuffled controls show no consistent alignment-specific benefit, and this conclusion holds under alternative risk thresholds and spatially preserving latent probes. The latent contains weak scene information that is largely redundant with the metric state. Matched state baselines and sample-correspondence controls are essential for evaluating foundation-model representations for physical-safety tasks.
